workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
rationale: Reset has priority over the watchdog's asynchronous set, so asserted reset always clears fault_q, and a fault still present at release is captured within a clock.

author_reading.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
author_reading.rationale: The reset is checked first in the asynchronous block, so an asserted reset always forces fault_q to zero and the watchdog set takes effect only after release.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: Reset is first in the branch, so rst_ni clears fault_q with priority over the watchdog set. The asynchronous set from wdog_fault_i is the intended fault latch. RDC-026 discloses the set and clear mix as a review item.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: Reset priority clears fault_q during overlap, but releasing reset while the watchdog stays asserted does not trigger the block. The asynchronous fault remains unreported until the next clock.

settlement.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
settlement.rationale: A is right. B's scenario (the watchdog still high at reset release) leaves fault_q clear only until the next clock in simulation, while a set/reset cell sets it immediately. Either way the fault is captured and no state is lost. RDC-026 may still report the set/clear mix as a review item.
